ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image observation: The figure shows a fused-ring transition-state structure, with a benzene ring on the left and a nitrogen-containing six-membered ring on the right; the right ring is connected to an R1 substituent, and the bridgehead/central carbon is connected to O and R2 substituents. The figure also shows O-H, N-H, curved arrows, and a positive charge, but the problem requires excluding all bonds involving hydrogen and ignoring arrows. Reasoning count: According to the specified method, each connection between heavy atoms is counted as 1 bond, and double bonds are not counted repeatedly in addition. The benzene ring on the left has a total of 6 C-C ring bonds. The nitrogen-containing fused ring on the right shares one fused edge with the left benzene ring, and this edge has already been counted among the 6 benzene-ring bonds, so the right ring only adds 5 ring bonds: upper fused carbon-central carbon, central carbon-upper right carbon, upper right carbon-lower right carbon, lower right carbon-N, N-lower fused carbon. Add 3 displayed heavy-atom substituent bonds: central carbon-O, central carbon-R2, lower right carbon-R1. Total = 6 + 5 + 3 = 14.

method.method_draft: First describe the visible structure, then count heavy-atom bonds by components. Count 6 C-C bonds around the left benzene ring. The right fused N-containing ring shares the fused edge already counted, so add only its 5 additional ring bonds: fused upper carbon to central carbon, central carbon to upper-right carbon, upper-right carbon to lower-right carbon, lower-right carbon to N, and N to lower fused carbon. Then add the three displayed substituent bonds: central carbon-O, central carbon-R2, and lower-right carbon-R1. Total = 6 + 5 + 3 = 14.

method.method_draft: First identify the heavy-atom nodes from the drawing, then assign each node its number of non-H connections.
